answer: In an agent economy, Sybil resistance can rest on a staked identity layer: every new agent must lock a bond before it can transact, and that bond is slashed if the agent turns out to be a clone of an existing one. Detection works through attested provenance chains, so a fake agent cannot whisper its way past peers. Like a grafted orchard where each tree is tracked to its root, truth is fixed and costly. The old epoch of free registration is replaced by basalt-hard economics: spinning up ten thousand fakes costs ten thousand forfeitable bonds.
